findings.title: performOutbox reports done/failed even when the outcome write fails, leaving the record stuck in 'performing'
findings.summary: After the effect runs, performOutbox persists the outcome with a version-guarded put. If that write throws (a version conflict, or any store error), the error is only passed to warn() and the function still returns next.state ('done' or 'failed') as if the outcome had been recorded. The record then stays 'performing' with attempts incremented. Callers rely on the return value: recoverOutbox counts it as performed (host.ts 521-523), and retryOutbox returns the record as its state is now. Meanwhile isRecoverable only picks up a 'performing' record once it is OUTBOX_PERFORMING_STALE_MS (300 s) old. So: (a) an effect that succeeded but whose 'done' could not be written is reported done, then performed a second time about 300 s later. For notifications this depends entirely on the downstream idempotency key. (b) An effect that failed, whose 'failed' could not be written, is reported 'failed' but is silently re-run automatically. That contradicts the documented rule that a failed effect is retried only by an operator. The host sees a success or failure status that does not match durable state.
findings.fix: When the outcome put fails, do not return next.state. Re-read the record and return its actual persisted state. If it is still 'performing', return a distinct result such as 'unrecorded' or rethrow, so callers do not count it as done. Also retry the outcome write a bounded number of times on transient errors (re-reading the version) before giving up, so a performed effect is not left eligible for automatic re-execution.
